# Epstein disclosure workstream — primary-source research memo
Research date: November 7, 2026 (Asia/Tokyo). Independent research support; not an official congressional finding.

## Direct correction for the landing page
The new Massie proposal concerns **state attorneys general and other authorized state officials**, not the **U.S. Department of State**. Give this workstream a neutral label: **“Epstein records: disclosure, survivor protection and enforcement.”** Do not label everyone appearing in files a perpetrator or present a list of suspected crimes as established guilt.

## Law versus proposal

### Existing law
**Epstein Files Transparency Act, Public Law 119-38, 139 Stat. 656–658 (November 19, 2025), originally H.R. 4405.** Section 2 directs the Attorney General to publish covered DOJ/FBI/U.S. Attorneys' Office records in searchable, downloadable form within 30 days, subject to the Act’s restrictions. It is not a transfer to the State Department. Covered subjects include investigations, travel, financial networks, charging decisions, agreements and records destruction. Section 2(c) protects victim-identifying/private material, CSAM, certain ongoing-investigation material, violence imagery and properly classified information. Section 3 requires a report to both Judiciary Committees. Privacy safeguards do not justify suppressing records solely for political sensitivity. Authority: https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/PLAW-119publ38/html/PLAW-119publ38.htm (sections 2–3; retrieval ref turn96view1).

### New House bill
**H.R. 9694, Epstein Files Transparency Act II, 119th Congress, introduced July 15, 2026 by Thomas Massie with Ro Khanna and Teresa Leger Fernández.** The official introduced bill was referred to House Judiciary. Its proposed new section 4 would provide enforcement actions for state AGs/DAs/authorized officers, victims and specified Members; expedited treatment; victim access to their own records with other victims protected; access for state investigations with sealing/protective requirements; and secure, court-governed classified review. Proposed congressional requests have response deadlines. This is proposed authority, not an already available access entitlement. The text’s references to criminal provisions retain the applicable mental-state requirements; it does not automatically convict an official.
Sources: https://www.govinfo.gov/app/details/BILLS-119hr9694ih (retrieval ref turn96search0); https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/BILLS-119hr9694ih/html/BILLS-119hr9694ih.htm (proposed section 4(a)–(f); retrieval ref turn98view1).

### Senate counterpart and status limit
**S. 5005, Epstein Files Transparency Act II**, introduced July 15, 2026 by Jeff Merkley with Ben Ray Luján; read twice and referred to Senate Judiciary. Official source: https://www.govinfo.gov/app/details/BILLS-119s5005is (retrieval ref turn101view0).
As of this research, the latest official bill-stage material verified for these measures is introduced/referred, dated July 15, 2026. No enactment of EFTA II was verified. Congress.gov’s bill and all-actions pages failed retrieval; GovInfo’s November 3, 2026 index still identifies these bill numbers, but an index alone is not a substitute for complete action history. Recheck the complete action feed before any future status publication. Index: https://www.govinfo.gov/app/details/CRI-2026/CRI-2026-EPSTEIN-FILES-TRANSPARENCY-ACT-II (turn96search4).

## Record integrity and privacy
DOJ’s disclosure page itself warns that personal information may have been released inadvertently and identifies existing grand-jury, court-order and victim-protection redactions. Public hosting is not proof that an individual record is safe to republish. Do not mirror bulk sensitive files, identify survivors, embed explicit material or feed raw sensitive records into public agents. The research task should extract publication metadata and legally reviewed, non-sensitive propositions. Record a source allegation as an allegation; a name, contact, flight entry or public tip does not by itself establish conduct or guilt.
Source: https://www.justice.gov/epstein/doj-disclosures (privacy notice and Court Records note, retrieval ref turn98view3).

DOJ reported a large production on January 30, 2026; the announcement is the agency’s account of its own compliance, not an independent completeness audit. Sponsors separately dispute DOJ’s compliance. The website must attribute these competing positions rather than adopt either as adjudicated fact.
Agency account: https://www.justice.gov/opa/pr/department-justice-publishes-35-million-responsive-pages-compliance-epstein-files (turn94search5).
Sponsor position: https://massie.house.gov/news/documentsingle.aspx?DocumentID=395849 (July 15, 2026, turn96view0). Use the bill text for operative provisions, not the press-release summary.

## Bounded oversight questions and research tickets
These are proposed legislative/administrative oversight questions, not findings of criminal liability.

1. **EFTA-DISCLOSURE-001 — Release accounting.** Compare the statutory categories against DOJ’s public release index and reports to Congress. Output a category-level table of dated releases, stated withholdings, source locations and gaps; do not invent the size of missing records.
2. **EFTA-PRIVACY-002 — Survivor-protection process.** Compare official redaction instructions with statute/court-protection requirements using non-sensitive policy materials. Report process deficiencies without reproducing the protected content.
3. **EFTA-PRESERVATION-003 — Records integrity.** Locate official retention, classification and destruction-accounting policies and lawful published records of relevant decisions. Separate missing documentation from proof of deliberate destruction.
4. **EFTA-ENFORCEMENT-004 — Bill comparison.** Compare current law, H.R. 9694 and S. 5005 section by section; label every proposed access, standing or remedy provision. Human counsel reviews statutory interactions before operational advice.
5. **EFTA-COORDINATION-005 — Institutional roles.** Map House Judiciary, Senate Judiciary and independently authorized state enforcement roles; no automatic dossier transfer and no promise of unredacted access under a pending bill.

Every ticket needs a legislative question, authorized public sources, prohibited sensitive data, source/quote pinpoints, counterevidence, a worker, a separate verifier and a human publication owner. The public output is a research question or verified proposition, not a prosecution recommendation generated by an agent.

## Broader investigation-topic taxonomy
Suggested topics expand the financial-corruption blueprint without asserting that the administration or any named person committed each offense.

| Public label | Bounded oversight question | Source hook |
|---|---|---|
| Financial conflicts and official decisions | Are disclosure, recusal and waiver systems adequate for covered officials? Do not assume a particular conflict statute applies to every office. | 18 U.S.C. § 208; official text https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?edition=prelim&hl=false&req=granuleid%3AUSC-prelim-title18-section208 (turn103search1). |
| Gifts, influence and contracting | Are controls sufficient to detect and prevent corrupt exchanges or improper influence? A financial connection alone proves no corrupt agreement. | 18 U.S.C. § 201; official text https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?req=%28title%3A18+section%3A201+edition%3Aprelim) (turn103search2). |
| Federal spending and procurement | Do payment, audit and contracting controls detect materially false claims? Distinguish waste, civil liability and criminal fraud. | 31 U.S.C. § 3729; official text https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?edition=prelim&num=0&req=granuleid%3AUSC-prelim-title31-section3729 (turn103search0). |
| Records, disclosure and institutional accountability | Are agencies creating and preserving adequate records, applying release rules consistently and documenting decisions? | 44 U.S.C. § 3101 and Chapter 31; National Archives https://www.archives.gov/about/laws/fed-agencies.html (turn103search3). |
| Epstein disclosure and survivor protection | Is the enacted disclosure regime being implemented, and what remedies or safeguards need legislative revision? | Public Law 119-38; pending H.R. 9694/S. 5005, above. |

This is an expandable topic index, not “all crimes.” Crypto flows, emoluments, foreign influence, state nexus and hospitality/real-property issues remain existing financial-research subtopics; legal application and underlying facts require their own primary-source packets.

## UX recommendation
Do not require an arrival pop-up asking whether “the House should investigate crimes by the administration.” It presupposes the conclusion and interrupts the intended congressional user. Put an optional, non-blocking link beneath the simple three-step diagram: **“Explore oversight questions.”** Topic cards should say **question / public source / committee role / next research task**, with expandable evidence and authority. Keep public opinion polling separate from official workflow and do not imply that a poll supplies investigative authority.
